subject: DataHarbor: perf discovery — streaming & context window implications

From: Alicia Park <a.park@dataharbor.io>

Subject: Re: DataHarbor perf discovery — summary and clarifications

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and a couple clarifying questions so we can finalize scope for the POC.

Summary of DH requirements (from our side):
- Primary UX: live agent-assist inside our analytics console. We need token-level streaming so agents see partial responses as they generate.
- Typical prompt size: ~8K tokens historical context (multiple docs + conversation), plus a 500–1,500 token query. We expect up to ~12K input tokens in the heaviest cases.
- Expected output: usually short (100–600 tokens), but sometimes long-form summaries up to 2,000 tokens for daily digest generation.
- Concurrency: peak 80 concurrent agent sessions during peak hours, baseline 25.
- Throughput target: sustain ~40 qps steady during peak bursts, with spikes to 70 qps for short windows.
- Latency targets: interactive streaming is a priority — we want first-token streaming within 250–400ms for typical short queries; full-output latency SLOs are secondary but would like end-to-end below 3.5s for outputs under 300 tokens.

Questions for Redwood:
1) With a 12K input + streaming enabled, what are the recommended model families / quantization profiles to meet the first-token streaming target?
2) How does continuous KV cache behavior change with frequent session switches (agents hop between users)? Any guidance for cache TTL or warm-start strategies?
3) What throughput envelope should we plan for per-GPU for 12K contexts with streaming enabled?

Attachments: DH_Data_Profile.xlsx (workload distribution + sample prompts). Call recording: linked in call_recording_link.txt.

Next steps: would like a short write-up from your side outlining realistic SLOs and a test plan for the POC by next Tue (6/22).

— Alicia
Product & Integrations, DataHarbor

Alicia — thanks for the clear notes and the attachment. High-level replies inline and an initial plan below.

Inline answers:
1) Model / quantization: for a 12K input + streaming we usually recommend the following options (tradeoff summary):
   - L-series 16K variant (fp16) on A100/H100 for lowest latency; streaming first-token should hit ~150–300ms p50 on short queries and p95 depends on output size.
   - Quantized 4-bit (q4) variants can be viable if you accept slightly higher decode CPU (and potentially a wider p95). q4 with KV cache friendly layout reduces memory and often increases concurrent session density.
   - If strict first-token p50/p95 is required for short queries, prioritize fp16 pinned capacity for the hot path and use quantized variants for lower-priority batched jobs (daily digests).
2) KV cache & session switches: frequent session switching will drop cold cache costs. Recommended approach: keep a small warm cache for the top N active users per GPU (LRU based), and use fast rehydrate from a lightweight prefix cache stored in Redis to cut warm-up to single-digit ms per request when possible. Session affinity (sticky routing for short-lived sessions) helps a lot.
3) Per-GPU throughput estimate (very approximate):
   - With 12K context + streaming on H100, expect ~8–12 streaming qps per GPU for interactive short outputs (100–300 tokens) when prioritizing low-latency tails.
   - If you accept slightly higher p95 (and use batching), you can push to ~15–20 qps per GPU.

Initial POC plan (deliverables):
- SLO proposal doc from Redwood (this will include p50/p95 targets, recommended model variants, and a test harness plan).
- Micro-benchmark: 3 scenario tests — (A) interactive short queries (avg 200 tokens out), (B) long-form summaries (avg 1,500 tokens out), (C) mixed workload with session churn.
- Canary configuration for first 2 weeks: dedicated small pool (2–4 GPUs) pinned to fp16 model for hot traffic + quantized pool for background batch jobs.

Action items:
- Redwood: write SLO doc + per-scenario throughput estimates and proposed test harness by Tue 2027-06-22 (Laura/Prio: laura_bennett + priyom_das).
- DataHarbor: confirm sample prompts in the attached spreadsheet and indicate which 10 customers to include in the POC sample set.

I'll follow up with the SLO draft this afternoon and a calendar invite for a technical run-through early next week to align on test data.

Best,

Alicia — quick update on the SLO doc and a couple of clarifications that will affect measurement:

1) How often do agents request full historical recomputes vs. incremental context? If full recomputes happen frequently, the KV cache warm-up cost will dominate and we'll recommend pre-warming during handoff windows.
2) For streaming UX, are partial tokens allowed to be truncated or do you need guaranteed complete tokens at each partial update? This affects chunking and rate-limits on the encoder side.

Planned SLO bullets for the draft:
- Target: first-stream-token p50 <= 250ms, p95 <= 450ms (hot path fp16).
- E2E: typical short reply (<= 300 tokens) median <= 900ms, p95 <= 3.5s.
- Throughput baseline: design to sustain 40 qps across cluster with headroom for 2x spike for 120s bursts.
- Concurrency policy: soft admission at 60% cluster utilization, hard at 95%.

We will attach a simple load recipe and - if DH provides a 48-hour trace - we'll derive a target distribution to run in our harness. Rafael — sending the calendar invite for the technical run-through Monday.

Thanks,
Priyo
Performance & Solutions, Redwood
